blindSummary:
This state/province recorded zero trans killings in 2024 but jumped to 4 in 2025 — the sharpest deterioration in the national monitoring dataset. Against a population of ~3.5 million, four cases yield roughly 1.14 killings per million per year, the highest per-capita rate among all 27 states/provinces in 2025 and about three times the national ~0.38 per million. The dossier cautions against reading a single-year zero as safety and notes the volatility.

The exposure is rate-driven rather than absolute: its 2025 count is lower than the regional leader's (4 versus 8) but its per-capita risk runs higher, placing this state/province among the worst units in the country for a given visitor despite modest raw numbers. It sits within the country's worst-affected region, which absorbed 38 of 80 national killings in 2025.

No state/province-level statutory restriction or unique legal finding applies; the risk is purely a violence-rate signal. With small absolute numbers a single incident dramatically shifts the picture, and the volatility suggests the environment can turn rapidly.
blindSourceSummaries: Regional news portal write-up (27 Jan 2025) of the trans-movement association's 2024 dossier: 122 killings of trans and travesti people (16% down from 145 in 2023, near the 2008-2024 average of 125/year), five victims were human-rights defenders, 95.9% of victims travestis/trans women, with systematic under-counting because official bodies do not properly record LGBTQIA+ victims — the basis for this state/province appearing with zero recorded killings in 2024 before jumping to 4 in 2025.

National news report on the 9th association dossier (2025 data): 80 killings nationwide, the 18th straight year atop the global tally; the state ranking places two regional leaders top with 8 each while this state/province and another appear with 4 each — the jump from a 2024 zero makes it the sharpest deterioration in the dataset; the worst-affected region recorded 38 of the 80 killings.
